title: In situ cyclodehydration of iminodiacetic acid into 2,5-diketopiperazine-1,4-diacetate in lanthanide-based coordination polymers

synthesis.procedure: Iminodiacetic acid, oxalic acid, Dy2O3 and HNO3 were stirred in water at room temperature, sealed in a 25 mL Teflon-lined stainless-steel container and heated at 180 °C for 100 h. The container was cooled to 100 °C at 3 °C h−1 and held for 16 h, then cooled further at 5 °C h−1. Colourless crystals were collected.
synthesis.vessel_or_method: Hydrothermal synthesis in a sealed 25 mL Teflon-lined stainless-steel container
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Cooled to 100 °C at 3 °C h−1, held for 16 h, then cooled further at 5 °C h−1; colourless block crystals collected.

properties.summary: The effective magnetic moment decreases on cooling; the authors attribute the sharper low-temperature decrease mainly to weak antiferromagnetic coupling between Dy(III) ions and partly to ligand-field splitting.

measurements.name: Effective magnetic moment per molecule
measurements.conditions: Room temperature; temperature-dependent measurement at 1000 Oe

source_locations.location: Introduction; structural discussion; notes and references, analytical data
Magnetic-properties paragraph; ESI Fig. S3 cited in main text

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: Oxalate links Dy(H2O) units into one-dimensional chains. The in situ-generated 2,5-diketopiperazine-1,4-diacetate ligand connects adjacent chains into layers, and additional carboxylate coordination joins the layers into a three-dimensional framework. Each ligand coordinates six Dy(III) ions.
